verdicts.reason: Quote states a CDC tool run reports zero crossings (TEST-016); verified by tool run, not simulation. check=none fits.

Reset is asserted asynchronously and deasserted synchronously; the release is provided by the SoC reset controller, so it is an input assumption, not a DUT behaviour. Scenario can exercise reset assertion/release; not assertion-checkable on DUT outputs. Actor is the SoC (system) and check should be scenario.
Rule is right (all flops async reset, FSMs IDLE, regs 0), but the actor is the bridge/DUT, not master. Internal register values are checkable via reset-time behaviour/outputs.

Quote states outputs after reset: opcode 000, address 0, data 0, valid 0. The bridge is the TL-UL host/requester driving these outputs, so actor master is plausible; checkable every cycle from interface signals while in reset state. Keep as is except check should be both, as reset must be exercised by a scenario.

o_tlul_d_ready becoming 1 at the first edge after reset release is checkable from interface signals, but it is driven by the bridge as the TL-UL D channel receiver (host side). Reset must also be exercised, so check should be both.

Abandoning an in-progress transfer on reset is a system-level behaviour that needs a scenario (reset mid-transfer). Not checkable by a per-cycle assertion on interface signals alone since the SoC resets the peers.
Quote states the IP is in the always-on domain with no isolation/retention/power sequencing; nothing to simulate. check=none is right.

duplicates.reason: Not merged in fact: they differ in signal and condition (outputs after reset vs o_tlul_d_ready at first edge after release).
